title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-04-15
content:
Serving runtime weekly update (kernel work, KV cache, batching) — Week ending 2026-04-15

Owner: Alex Chen
Contributors: Priya Kapoor, Evan Martinez, Sofia Li, Maya Johnson
Status: In review

Summary
- This week focused on three parallel efforts: kernel micro-optimizations for attention matmul, KV cache correctness and eviction heuristics, and dynamic batching improvements to reduce tail latency for short requests.
- We merged the first pass of the attention kernel rewrite (PR #4321) and rolled it out to the canary pool for internal load testing. Initial numbers look promising but uncovered a memory regression on >16k context sequences.

Kernel work
- What we did:
  - Merged attention kernel rewrite (PR #4321). Replaces tiled GEMM paths with a fused attention kernel on Ampere/NextGen GPUs.
  - Added runtime autodetection of tensor layout to pick the new kernel only when shapes match the fast path.
  - Microbenchmarked across representative models (gpt-like 2.7B, 7B, and 13B) and sequence lengths 64/256/1024.
- Results (canary):
  - 7B model: mean token p99 latency down ~18% for seq=256 workloads.
  - 2.7B: small improvements (~7%) for seq<=64, no regression.
  - 13B: improvements at seq=1024 (~12% mean), but observed memory regression at seq>16k on some cards (OOB allocation).
- Blockers & next steps:
  - Memory regression tracepoint points to incorrect scratch allocation when fused kernel falls back to non-fused path; Priya to file INF-3421 with repro and heap traces.
  - Action: rollback fused kernel on 4 nodes with constrained memory; keep canary on others. Plan to land a fix next week that adjusts scratch allocation accounting and adds unit test coverage.

KV cache (prefix/KV)
- What we did:
  - Continued rollout of prefix-aware KV-cache eviction policy (LRU + affinity for hot prefixes).
  - Implemented metrics for per-prefix hit rate and cache churn; dashboard added to Console (route: serving-runtime/kv-cache).
- Results:
  - For production-internal trace workload, cache hit rate improved from 62% -> 78% for common system prompts, reducing average tokens computed per request by ~0.22 tokens (measured across 48h sample).
  - Observed improved tail latency at p95 for multi-turn chat use-cases (~14% improvement).
- Issues:
  - Rare correctness bug where eviction retained stale KV shards after model reload if reload happened concurrently with eviction. Repro steps in Slack thread; Evan has a minimal repro.
  - Mitigation: conservative lock around shard swap landed (hotfix) to prevent stale reads; this increases contention slightly — monitoring CPU usage.
- Next steps:
  - Add integration test that simulates concurrent reload+evict; schedule for next sprint.
  - Priya to prototype a shard-granular generation-id scheme to allow lock-free validation.

Batching improvements
- What we did:
  - Landed dynamic batching window change: adaptive max wait reduces batching delay for short requests by lowering window to 8ms when queue depth is low.
  - Introduced early-flush for single-request low-latency SLO routes (configurable per-route in rollout).
- Results:
  - Short-seq (<64 tokens) p50 latency improved by ~22% across canary routes.
  - Overall throughput maintained for bursty traffic due to fast up-scaling of batch size when queue depth rises.
- Risks:
  - For extremely bursty tiny requests (many 1-token requests), CPU overhead of early-flush can increase context-switching; observed 3–5% CPU increase on small instance types.
  - Plan: add heuristics to disable early-flush on instance types where CPU cost exceeds threshold.

Operational metrics and deploy notes
- Canary rollout (10% of serving capacity) ongoing since 2026-04-12. Observability: added dashboards for kernel memory, per-prefix KV-hit, and batching window histograms.
- Key metrics to watch this week:
  - kernel_memory_oob_count (should be 0) — currently elevated on 4 nodes.
  - kv_cache_hit_rate_by_prefix — target >=75% for common prefixes.
  - p95_latency_short_seq_route — aim to reduce by 10% week-over-week.

Action items and owners
- Priya: debug kernel memory regression, file INF-3421 with heap traces and repro. (Due 2026-04-18)
- Evan: add concurrent-reload+evict integration test; coordinate with SRE to reproduce load pattern. (Due 2026-04-22)
- Sofia: tune early-flush heuristics by instance type; run A/B on small instance fleet. (Due 2026-04-21)
- Maya: validate KV metrics dashboard and add alert for kv_cache_stale_eviction > 0. (Due 2026-04-17)

Notes / discussion points
- We should decide if fused attention kernel becomes opt-in per model (via model-profile) to avoid broad rollback in case of regressions. Pros: safer rollout, cons: increases profile management surface area.
- Suggest adding a quick smoke test that runs on every kernel PR that targets >8k context to catch OOBs earlier in CI.

Questions for leadership
- Budget: estimated additional test GPU hours required next sprint to validate kernel fixes across model matrix ~ 350 GPU-hours. Need approval to reserve shared cluster time.
- Product: Should we enable prefix-aware KV caching by default for all hosted-api routes that have multi-turn enabled, or keep it opt-in while we stabilize?

Appendix: Links and refs
- Kernel PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4321
- KV design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/KV+Cache+Design
- Jira: INF-3421 (kernel mem regression)
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime-kv (thread ts: 1711234567.123456)

End of weekly update.
